voci.titolo: Treasury Yields Extend Past Month’s Slide as Oil Prices Drop
voci.riassunto: Treasuries rose, building on their biggest monthly advance in more than two years, as tumbling oil prices eased concern about inflation pressure leading to additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes.

voci.titolo: Hedge Funds Back SEC Push to Ease Rules on EU Bond Futures
voci.riassunto: The Securities and Exchange Commission should add the European Union to a four-decade old list of exempted issuers, a move that would ease restrictions on US investor access to the bloc’s new bond futures market, according to a group representing hedge funds.

voci.titolo: Gold’s Faded Haven Allure Hinges on Deficit, Inflation Fears
voci.riassunto: As gold heads toward its worst annual loss in more than a decade, investors are gauging the odds a political shift in the US will restore the precious metal’s haven allure.

voci.titolo: Oracle Seeks $20 Billion for AI Growth as Meta Weighs New Debt
voci.riassunto: For almost three months, Big Tech companies didn’t borrow in the US bond market after they spooked investors with a debt binge in the hundreds of billions of dollars. Now they’re flooding in again.

voci.titolo: Romania Raises €4.5 Billion in New Government’s First Bond Sale
voci.riassunto: Romania tapped international debt markets for the first time after the country approved a new government to overcome more than five months of political turmoil.

voci.titolo: South Korea targets 'world's highest performance' sovereign AI model in record new budget
voci.riassunto: The 2027 budget will rise 12.8% to 820.9 trillion won, and will include a 21.3 trillion won investment into semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centers.

voci.titolo: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts
voci.riassunto: The euro zone showed surprising resilience, but weak productivity, industrial competitiveness challenges and demographic pressures remain, analysts said.

voci.titolo: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates
voci.riassunto: The personal consumption expenditures price index was projected to increase 0.5% in September for an annual rate of 3.7%, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

voci.titolo: Analysis: Kevin Warsh is keeping Wall Street guessing. It may be his most powerful tool
voci.riassunto: The new chairman made clear he leans toward higher interest rates, but left himself options depending on how the data comes in.

voci.titolo: The politics of President Lagarde's European Central Bank early exit — and who could replace her
voci.riassunto: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down on Feb. 7 next year, she announced Thursday.

voci.titolo: European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%
